title: Reflexive verbs and daily routine
description: mi, ti, si, ci, vi, si with the verb; describing a day.
objectives: Conjugate reflexive verbs with the correct pronoun.

blocks.text: A reflexive infinitive ends in *-si*: *svegliarsi* (to wake up), *sedersi* (to sit down), *vestirsi* (to get dressed). Remove *-si*, put back the *-e*, and you have an ordinary verb that conjugates normally (*svegliare*, *sedere*, *vestire*).

blocks.title: Pronoun + conjugated verb
blocks.text: Each person takes its reflexive pronoun before the verb: *mi, ti, si, ci, vi, si*.

blocks.title: Position of the pronoun
blocks.text: Before the conjugated verb (*mi alzo*), after *non* (*non mi alzo*). With an infinitive it attaches to the end: *alzarmi, alzarti, alzarsi…* — *Devo alzarmi* or *Mi devo alzare*.

blocks.title: Not always 'oneself'
blocks.text: Some reflexives really mean 'oneself' (*lavarsi* = to wash oneself). Many simply correspond to an English intransitive verb: *svegliarsi* = to wake up, *addormentarsi* = to fall asleep, *chiamarsi* = to be called, *divertirsi* = to have fun.

blocks.title: Body parts take the article, not a possessive
blocks.text: *Mi lavo le mani* = I wash my hands. The reflexive pronoun already shows whose hands they are.

items: *Mi sveglio alle sette.* — I wake up at seven.
*Mi alzo e mi lavo.* — I get up and wash.
*Mi vesto e faccio colazione.* — I get dressed and have breakfast.
*La sera mi siedo sul divano e leggo.* — In the evening I sit on the sofa and read.
*Alle dieci mi addormento.* — At ten I fall asleep.

examples.it: Come ti chiami? — Mi chiamo Sara.
examples.en: What's your name? — My name is Sara.
We have fun at the seaside.
I sit down on the chair.

examples.it: Non mi alzo presto la domenica.
examples.en: I don't get up early on Sundays.

exercises.prompt: Conjugate *alzarsi* in the present (include the pronoun).

mistakes.message: si is for lui/lei and loro. With noi use ci.

exercises.explanation: sedere has the stressed stem sied-: mi siedo.
Body parts: reflexive pronoun + article, no possessive.

mistakes.message: Grammatically possible but unidiomatic. Italian says Mi lavo le mani.

exercises.text: La mattina io {0} (svegliarsi) alle sette, {1} (vestirsi) e faccio colazione. La sera i bambini {2} (addormentarsi) presto.
exercises.explanation: mi sveglio, mi vesto, si addormentano.

summary: Reflexive infinitives end in -si; conjugate the base verb and add mi, ti, si, ci, vi, si before it.
With an infinitive the pronoun attaches: alzarmi.
Many reflexives translate as simple English verbs (wake up, fall asleep, be called).
Mi lavo le mani: article, not possessive.
